hunks.baseline: The battle between two forces, waged around the canyon, could be summed up in four characters:
hunks.sol: The battle raging around the canyon could be summed up in one phrase: advance and retreat.

hunks.baseline: Advance and retreat.
The fighting was that fierce, and everyone on both sides had put their lives on the line.
hunks.sol: Neither side could gain ground for long. Everyone fought with their lives on the line.

hunks.baseline: Some fought for a faith they had believed in all their lives—a faith they couldn’t even imagine might be false.
hunks.sol: Some fought for a faith they had held all their lives, one they could not even imagine was false. Others fought for convictions just as firm.

hunks.baseline: Others fought for their unshakable convictions.
It was a clash of faith and conviction, and at the same time, a holy war.
hunks.sol: It was a clash of faith and conviction. To those fighting it, a holy war.

hunks.baseline: But in a place awash with blood and death, religion no longer mattered.
hunks.sol: But amid so much blood and death, whether anyone was religious no longer mattered.

hunks.baseline: Demons.
hunks.sol: *Demons.*

hunks.baseline: They were human beings with the same appearance, but each held a different standard for good and evil. Their eyes met between the blades lunging toward one another, burning with murderous intent.
hunks.sol: They were all human, yet each side had its own idea of good and evil. Their eyes met across the blades they thrust at one another, burning with the will to kill.

hunks.baseline: Swords and sabers clashed. A sharp screech rang out, and vivid blue sparks flew. Blood spurted amid broken shouts, impossible to tell who had cried out.
hunks.sol: Sword met saber. Blue sparks flew with a sharp screech. Blood spurted amid ragged shouts, impossible to tell who had cried out.

hunks.baseline: A panicked shout and a roar of impact collided. A tank stared at an arrowhead that had pierced halfway through his enormous tower shield, right in front of his face, and sucked in a breath.
hunks.sol: A warning shout mingled with the roar of impact. A tank stared at the arrowhead protruding halfway through his enormous tower shield, inches from his face, and swallowed.

hunks.baseline: If he’d raised his shield just a little—just a fraction—later, he would have died.
hunks.sol: If he’d raised his shield just a fraction later, he would have died.

hunks.baseline: But Hunters were closer to death than anyone. And everyone here had survived countless brushes with death just like this one.
hunks.sol: But Hunters lived closer to death than anyone. Everyone here had survived countless brushes with it.

hunks.baseline: The tank grabbed the arrow and snapped it in two, then shouted in a hoarse voice.
hunks.sol: The tank grabbed the arrow and snapped it, then shouted hoarsely.

hunks.baseline: Countless flashes rained down. Blades flashed, heavy clubs swung, and even fanatics on the verge of death forced themselves upright and charged.
hunks.sol: Countless flashes rained down. Sharp blades and heavy clubs struck, and even fanatics on the verge of death forced themselves upright and charged.

hunks.baseline: The impacts pounding their shields were so immense that even the veteran tanks, hardened by years of combat, thought of death.
hunks.sol: The impacts hammered the shields so hard that even veteran tanks, hardened by years of combat, thought they might die.

hunks.baseline: They squeezed out the strength they had left in their shouts and clenched their teeth until they felt ready to break. Their feet slid backward under the pressure, carving deep furrows into the ground.
hunks.sol: They shouted to wring out the last of their strength and clenched their teeth until they felt ready to break. Their feet slid backward under the pressure, carving deep furrows in the ground.

hunks.baseline: The enemy had an overwhelming numerical advantage.
hunks.sol: The enemy had an overwhelming advantage in numbers.

hunks.baseline: It had been less than three hours since the battle against the monster army ended.
hunks.sol: Less than three hours had passed since the battle against the monster army. That fight had drained them in body and mind, and the fanatics were the worst opponents they could have faced now.

hunks.baseline: The strain of that fierce fight was eating away at their bodies and minds alike, and the fanatics they now faced were the worst possible opponents.
Ten thousand of them.
hunks.sol: Nearly ten thousand of them.

hunks.baseline: They kept charging even after their chests were cut open or their limbs were severed, their eyes alight with venom.
hunks.sol: They kept charging with their chests slashed open or their limbs severed.

hunks.baseline: More than thirty years ago, the Doppelganger had raised these fanatics somewhere in this barren desert, out of the world’s sight, under the name of the Prophet. Now they were monsters of another kind.
hunks.sol: More than thirty years ago, the Doppelganger had raised these fanatics somewhere in this barren desert, hidden from the world, under the name of the Prophet. They were monsters of another kind.

hunks.baseline: A sword blade bearing a faint aura pierced a chest and burst out the other side.
hunks.sol: A sword bearing a faint aura pierced a fanatic’s chest and emerged from his back.

hunks.baseline: It was a grievous wound. Even if he used a potion right away, there was no telling whether he’d live or die. Yet the fanatic whose chest had been pierced bared his blood-soaked teeth and smiled.
hunks.sol: Even a potion used immediately might not save him. Yet he bared his blood-soaked teeth and smiled.

hunks.baseline: The madness in that fading voice made the Hunter’s body seize up.
hunks.sol: The madness in that fading voice made the Hunter freeze.

hunks.baseline: A chill swept over him from head to toe.
But by the time he came to his senses, it was too late.
hunks.sol: A chill swept over him. By the time he came to his senses, it was too late.

hunks.baseline: A single whistle of air pierced his ear. At the same instant, his vision went dark.
hunks.sol: A sharp whistle cut past his ear. At the same instant, his vision went dark.

hunks.baseline: The Hunter who caught his falling comrade clenched his lips.
hunks.sol: The Hunter who caught his falling comrade bit his lip.

hunks.baseline: But the comrade with whom he had saved each other’s life time and again never answered.
hunks.sol: But the man who had saved his life time and again—and whose life he had saved in turn—did not answer.

hunks.baseline: The dagger had pierced him exactly between the eyes, taking his voice and his life at once.
hunks.sol: The dagger lodged squarely between Hans’s eyes had taken his voice and his life.

hunks.baseline: The Hunter’s eyes darkened as he laid down the body.
hunks.sol: The Hunter laid down the body, his gaze darkening.

hunks.baseline: The canyon was an ideal battlefield for facing a larger force, but no matter how efficiently they fought, casualties were unavoidable.
hunks.sol: The canyon was well suited to holding off a larger force, but even fighting as efficiently as they could, they could not avoid casualties.

hunks.baseline: Especially against madmen who thought of death as martyrdom.
hunks.sol: Especially against madmen who saw death as martyrdom.

hunks.baseline: It was just as their ranks were about to crumble before the wave of fanatics charging without regard for their lives—
hunks.sol: Their ranks were beginning to crumble before the wave of fanatics charging without regard for their lives when—

hunks.baseline: A fierce heat washed over everyone’s heads.
hunks.sol: Heat washed over everyone’s heads.

hunks.baseline: Before anyone could look up, a rain of fire came pouring down like a meteor shower, accompanied by a sharp whistle.
hunks.sol: Before anyone could look up, fire came pouring down like a meteor shower with a fierce whistle.

hunks.baseline: Dozens of balls of fire appeared above the Hunters and fell toward the battlefield, toward the fanatics who charged without end.
hunks.sol: Dozens of fireballs appeared above the Hunters and fell toward the battlefield, toward the fanatics who charged without end.

hunks.baseline: As everyone stared up at the sight, mouths hanging open, one name flashed through their minds.
hunks.sol: As everyone stared, mouths open, one name flashed through their minds.

hunks.baseline: The Grand Mage said to have received the blessing of mana. Among Grand Mages, he was the world’s greatest War Mage, proven so during the Great Cataclysm. At last, he was showing his true strength.
hunks.sol: The Grand Mage said to have been blessed by mana. The world’s greatest War Mage, whose power had been proven during the Great Cataclysm, was finally showing what he could do.

hunks.baseline: With a powerful area spell that could turn the tide of battle.
hunks.sol: A powerful area spell that could turn the tide of battle.

hunks.baseline: *That’s it. If he can do that…*
hunks.sol: *That’s it. With that…*

hunks.baseline: Every Hunter thought the same thing. No—they were certain of it.
hunks.sol: Every Hunter thought the same thing. No—they were certain.

hunks.baseline: With Jin Taekyung nowhere to be seen, Magic Johnson was their surest bet to lead them to victory.
hunks.sol: With Jin Taekyung nowhere to be seen, Magic Johnson was their surest path to victory.

hunks.baseline: At least, that was what they thought—until blue waves surged up from this parched land, where all there was in every direction was sand and stone.
hunks.sol: At least, they were certain until blue waves surged up from parched land that held nothing but sand and stone in every direction.

hunks.baseline: Dozens of voices rang as one. Spheres of water stacked upon spheres of water, rising into an enormous tidal wave.
hunks.sol: Dozens of voices rang as one. Spheres of water piled upon spheres of water and rose into an enormous tidal wave.

hunks.baseline: Two forces, opposites of one another, twisted together. They collided.
hunks.sol: The opposing forces met and mingled. Then they collided.

hunks.baseline: With a shockwave that shook everything within hundreds of meters, they exploded above the heads of the Hunters and fanatics.
hunks.sol: The impact shook the air for hundreds of meters around them as they exploded above the Hunters and fanatics.

hunks.baseline: “M-My God!”
hunks.sol: “O God!”

hunks.baseline: Someone screamed from beyond the steam that swept through the area on the wind.
hunks.sol: Screams rang out beyond the steam sweeping through the battlefield on the wind.

hunks.baseline: The thick steam blocked the view, leaving everyone unable to make out what had happened. But Magic Johnson, the one who had cast the spell, knew better than anyone.
hunks.sol: The thick steam blinded everyone to what had happened. But Magic Johnson, who had cast the spell, knew better than anyone.

hunks.baseline: *It was blocked. Almost completely.*
hunks.sol: *Blocked. Almost completely.*

hunks.baseline: He said almost because part of his Fire Storm had swallowed some of the fanatics. But he could tell the damage was far less than he had expected.
hunks.sol: Only almost because part of his Fire Storm had engulfed some fanatics. Even so, he could tell the damage was far less than he had expected.

hunks.baseline: Magic Johnson had seen them clearly: thirty mages under an ironclad escort.
hunks.sol: Magic Johnson had seen them clearly: thirty mages emerging under heavy guard.

hunks.baseline: Their turbans were pulled low over their brows. Every last one of them was A-rank, and, like him, a War Mage specialized in combat.
hunks.sol: Their turbans were pulled low. Every last one was A-rank and, like him, a War Mage specialized in combat.

hunks.baseline: There was no need to wonder who had created all that overwhelming power in front of him.
hunks.sol: He didn’t need to wonder who had built the force before him.

hunks.baseline: The Great Cataclysm had been a time of immense chaos. Thirty years was long enough for nature itself to change, and the desert must have been the perfect place to hide something.
hunks.sol: The Great Cataclysm had been a time of immense chaos. Thirty years was long enough for the landscape itself to change, and the desert was an ideal place to hide something.

hunks.baseline: So what Magic Johnson wanted to know wasn’t how the Doppelganger had gathered and trained them.
hunks.sol: How the Doppelganger had gathered and trained them was not what Magic Johnson wanted to know.

hunks.baseline: His question reached back to the beginning and end of all this.
hunks.sol: His question went to the beginning and end of it all.

hunks.baseline: *What on earth did you want that you prepared so thoroughly?*
hunks.sol: *What do you want badly enough to have prepared all this?*

hunks.baseline: But Magic Johnson’s question reached no one. Even if the Doppelganger had known what he was wondering, it wouldn’t have answered.
hunks.sol: But his question reached no one. Even if the Doppelganger had known what he was thinking, it would not have answered.

preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: No—it wouldn’t even have had time.
hunks.sol: No—it would not even have had time.

hunks.baseline: But despite his determination, Magic Johnson couldn’t move easily.
hunks.sol: But Magic Johnson could not move so easily.

hunks.baseline: Unlike monsters, the fanatics had been trained rigorously, and they knew what mattered most in this battle.
hunks.sol: Unlike monsters, the fanatics were thoroughly trained. They knew what mattered most in this battle.

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: They used their more-than-tenfold numbers to attack in rotating waves.
hunks.sol: They had more than ten times the Hunters’ numbers and used them to attack in rotating waves.

hunks.baseline: The two strongest members of their force—and its commanders—were under concentrated attack.
hunks.sol: The fanatics concentrated their attacks on the two strongest members of the Hunters’ force—the two who could also be called its commanders.

hunks.baseline: Arrows and magic rained down. No matter that Magic Johnson was a Grand Mage; attacks he couldn’t afford to take lightly kept flying in from every direction.
hunks.sol: Arrows and magic rained down. Even a Grand Mage like Magic Johnson could not afford to ignore the attacks coming without pause from every direction.

hunks.baseline: The Skeleton King was in the same situation.
hunks.sol: The Skeleton King was in much the same position.

hunks.baseline: The Bone Sword, made of bone, swept in smooth arcs.
hunks.sol: His Bone Sword swept in smooth arcs.

hunks.baseline: But before the bodies crumpling in sprays of blood could hit the ground, dazzling flashes cut through the falling bodies and shot toward the Skeleton King.
hunks.sol: But before the bodies crumpling in sprays of blood could hit the ground, dazzling flashes cut through them and shot toward him.

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: The Skeleton King was aghast. Since coming into this world, he’d never faced anyone this crazy. The fact that there were ten thousand of them made it all the more unbelievable.
hunks.sol: The Skeleton King was aghast. Since coming into this world, he had never encountered people this crazy.
Much less ten thousand of them.

hunks.baseline: The Skeleton King wielded the power of death, but even he was nearly overwhelmed by the endless wave of fanatics.
hunks.sol: He wielded the power of death, yet the endless wave of fanatics was nearly enough to overwhelm even him.

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: Everyone feared death. No—he himself, an undead monster, feared Erasure. It was a problem like a fate bestowed the moment one was born.
hunks.sol: Every human feared death. Even he, an undead monster, feared Erasure. That fear seemed as inevitable as being born.

hunks.baseline: So why weren’t the humans before him afraid to die?
hunks.sol: So why weren’t these humans afraid to die?

hunks.baseline: *These people are the real monsters…*
hunks.sol: *They’re the real monsters…*

hunks.baseline: But each time the Skeleton King took one down, three more came. When he took down three, ten showed up. And when he felled those, fanatics poured in from every direction, swinging the weapons in their hands.
hunks.sol: When he took one down, three more came. When he took down three, ten came. And when he felled those, fanatics rushed in from every direction, swinging their weapons.

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: A chilling sound of a blade slicing through flesh rang out, but naturally, there was no pain.
hunks.sol: A blade cut through him with a chilling sound. Naturally, he felt no pain.

hunks.baseline: The Skeleton King sighed as he looked at the sword that had pierced his chest.
hunks.sol: The Skeleton King sighed at the sword piercing his chest.

hunks.baseline: A bone shard shot from his turned wrist and pierced an enemy’s throat.
hunks.sol: He turned his wrist. A bone shard shot out and pierced his attacker’s throat.

hunks.baseline: With a gurgling sound, the fanatic fell. The Skeleton King kicked him hard, clearing some space. At that moment—
hunks.sol: As the fanatic fell with a wet gurgle, the Skeleton King kicked him hard to clear some space.

hunks.baseline: A dark shape flew toward him with a heavy whistle. The Skeleton King hurriedly caught it.
hunks.sol: A dark shape came flying toward him with a heavy whistle. He caught it in a hurry.

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: It coughed up blood. It was a human, and still alive.
hunks.sol: It coughed up blood. A human, still alive.

hunks.baseline: More than that, it was familiar.
hunks.sol: And one he knew.

hunks.baseline: There was no doubt. Though blood covered his entire body, the Skeleton King recognized him at once.
hunks.sol: There was no mistaking him, even covered head to toe in blood.

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: The Skeleton King had raised the undead monster with his magical power slowly running dry. He tapped the man’s cheek.
hunks.sol: The Skeleton King raised an undead monster with what little magical power he had left, then tapped the man’s cheek.

hunks.baseline: “Hey. Human with a fine-looking build. Can you hear me?”
hunks.sol: “Hey. You, the human who’s all looks. Can you hear me?”

hunks.baseline: *Cough.* Choi Minwoo spat up blood again, then answered in a voice on the verge of fading.
hunks.sol: *Cough.* Choi Minwoo spat up blood again and answered in a voice barely above a whisper.

hunks.baseline: “Good. We’re short on time, so listen carefully. You’re not going to die, so don’t worry. And even if you do, I’ll bring you back as an undead, so don’t—dammit. He passed out.”
hunks.sol: “Good. We’re short on time, so listen carefully. You’re not going to die, so don’t worry. Even if you do, I’ll bring you back as an undead, so there’s no need to—dammit. He passed out.”

hunks.baseline: The Skeleton King clicked his tongue and stood up, then added, almost as an afterthought:
hunks.sol: The Skeleton King clicked his tongue and stood. Then he added, almost as an afterthought, “Still, he held out remarkably well, all things considered. Don’t you think?”

hunks.baseline: “Well, he held out damn well, all things considered. Don’t you think?”
An aura slashed past the Skeleton King’s head instead of an answer.
hunks.sol: An aura swept past the Skeleton King’s head in place of an answer.

hunks.baseline: He watched blond hair flutter through the air, muttered a string of curses, then faced forward. Through the thick steam, he saw a man.
hunks.sol: He watched strands of blond hair drift down, muttered a string of curses, and looked ahead. A man stood beyond the thick steam.

hunks.baseline: “Not at all. He’s trash.”
hunks.sol: “Not at all. That bastard is trash.”

hunks.baseline: His hair was a mess, and a wound ran across his cheek.
hunks.sol: His hair was disheveled, and a wound crossed his cheek.

hunks.baseline: The Skeleton King gave a short laugh at the man’s eyes, burning with rage.
hunks.sol: The Skeleton King gave a quiet laugh at the fury in the man’s eyes.

hunks.baseline: “No matter how I look at it, he fought well. When he wakes up, I’ll have to praise him myself.”
hunks.sol: “No, I’d say he fought well. I’ll have to praise him myself when he wakes up.”

hunks.baseline: “You’ll find out when you die. Which of us was the demon.”
hunks.sol: “When you die, you’ll find out which of us was the demon.”

hunks.baseline: “Get in here, quick. Before someone scarier than me shows up.”
hunks.sol: “Come at me, then. Before someone scarier than me gets here.”
